Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked. this is only one component so in one file at all



Reasoning accordion (cot-message-chunk, cot-v5) featuring live step spinners, progress checkmarks, and dynamic height transitions.
use liquid glass
Rather than blurring whatever sits behind it, a Liquid Glass surface bends that content the way a real lens would, catches specular highlights that shift as you tilt the device, and adapts its own tint and shadow to whatever is passing underneath. Move the content, and the glass responds. It is closer to a simulated physical object than to a CSS effect.
The distinction that matters: glassmorphism blurs what is behind it, Liquid Glass refracts it. Add specular highlights that track device motion, tint and shadow that respond to the content passing underneath, and shapes that morph and merge into one another as the interface changes, and you have a material that is simulated per frame rather than declared once.

Practically: most of what gets posted online as “liquid glass” on the web is glassmorphism with better lighting. Genuine refraction in a browser needs displacement mapping or a shader, not backdrop-filter

többrétegű valós idejű fénytörő kompozíciós anyagrendszert UI elemekhez Apple platformokra. A komponensnek meg kell valósítania az adaptív áttetszőséget, az optikai fénytörést, a spekuláris kiemeléseket, a kromatikus effektusokat, a fénysűrűség-vezérelt színezést és a folyamatos sima alakzat-összeolvadást
Kezdd a mag réteg-hierarchia meghatározásával, amelyet minden üveg-elem futásidőben felépít:
•  Egy gyökér konténer réteg, amely a teljes effektus-vermet fogadja.
•  Egy opcionális magasabb szintű burkoló réteg, amely több elem-példányt kezel.
•  Egy elsődleges mintavételező réteg CABackdropLayer típusból, amely a WindowServer útvonalon keresztül rögzíti az elem mögötti tartalmat. Bővítsd ki ezt a réteget a következő tulajdonságokkal: tracksLuma (logikai érték, amely vezérli, hogy a réteg folyamatosan mintavételezi-e az alatta lévő fénysűrűséget), lumaSubrect (CGRect, amely a fénysűrűség-követéshez használt régiót határozza meg), allowsFilteredLuma (logikai érték, amely lehetővé teszi fekete vagy fehér átfedő réteg beállítását), és lumaUpdateRate (lebegőpontos érték, amely a fénysűrűség-frissítések időbeli simítását vezérli). Konfiguráld a réteget úgy, hogy window-server tudatos maradjon, és egyedi csoportnevet használjon a helyes kompozíciós elkülönítéshez.
•  A mintavételező rétegen belül egy SDF textúra-forrás réteg CASDFLayer típusból, amely az “@0” névvel van azonosítva. Ennek a rétegnek generálnia kell a tartalmazott geometria signed-distance-field ábrázolását és a megfelelő normáltérképet.
•  Az SDF textúra-forrás rétegen belül egy egyszerű CALayer konténer, amely egy vagy több CASDFElementLayer példányt tartalmaz. Minden CASDFElementLayer egyetlen alakzat geometriai leírását tárolja signed distance field formájában.
•  Két további testvér CASDFLayer példány az “@1” és “@2” nevekkel. Ezek a rétegek irányított üveg-kiemelés effektusokat kapnak, és mindegyik tartalmaz egy SDFPortalLayer-t, amely a primer CASDFElementLayer geometriáját tükrözi teljes újraraszterizálás nélkül.
•  Alkalmazz egy “glassBackground” nevű CAFilter-t az elsődleges CABackdropLayer-re. A szűrőnek az SDF normáltérkép textúrát az inputSourceSublayerName kulcson keresztül kell fogadnia, amely “@0”-ra van állítva, és végre kell hajtania a fénytörést, a Gauss-elmosódást, a vibrancy-beállítást, a tónusleképezést és a kromatikus diszperziót. További vibrantColorMatrix típusú szűrők alkalmazhatók a kiemelés-rétegekre színmátrix-tónusvezérléshez.
Valósítsd meg a következő privát-effektus osztályokat, amelyek az SDF feldolgozást konfigurálják:
•  CASDFOutputEffect, amely az alakzat-rétegeket backdrop-kompatibilis SDF textúrákká alakítja.
•  CASDFGlassHighlightEffect, amely irányfüggő élvilágítást generál a felületi normálok és egy konfigurálható fényirány alapján.
•  CASDFGlassDisplacementEffect, amely a fénytörési eltolás mértékét és lecsengését vezérli.
Minden SDF geometriát signed-distance függvényekkel kell definiálni. Biztosíts analitikus SDF primitíveket lekerekített téglalapokhoz (szuperellipszis támogatás opcionális), és valósíts meg egy sima-unió operátort, amely két SDF értéket és egy k keverési együtthatót fogad, folyamatos, paramétervezérelt alakzat-összeolvadást eredményezve. Vezesd le a felületi normálokat a kombinált SDF analitikus vagy véges-különbséges gradienseiből; ezek a normálok vezérlik mind a fénytörést, mind a spekuláris kiemelés-számításokat.
árnyékoló is kell, amely végrehajtja az optikai szimulációt. A fragment shadernek:
•  Mintavételeznie kell a CABackdropLayer-től kapott háttértextúrát.
•  Ki kell számítania a helyi SDF értéket és annak gradiensét minden fragmentumnál.
•  Ki kell számítania a fénytörési eltolásokat a Metal refract függvény használatával, független törésmutatókat támogatva a vörös, zöld és kék csatornákhoz a kromatikus aberráció előállításához.
•  Alkalmaznia kell Fresnel-stílusú élintenzitást a nézési szög koszinusza alapján.
•  Generálnia kell irányított spekuláris kiemeléseket, amelyek a felületi normálokra és egy dinamikus fényirányra reagálnak.
•  Végre kell hajtania mip-leképezett elmosódást, amelynek sugara az SDF felszínhez mért távolsága szerint modulálódik.
•  Be kell építenie az adaptív színezést a követett fénysűrűség-értékekből.
•  Ki kell adnia a végső színt helyes előszorzott alfával.
A rendszernek automatikusan adaptálnia kell az átlátszatlanságot, az elmosódás sugarát és a fénysűrűség-követés erősségét az elem mérete és az alatta lévő tartalom fénysűrűsége szerint. A nagyobb elemek erősebb szóródást és mélyebb árnyékokat kapnak; a görgetési él-régiók további elmosódást és átlátszatlanság-csökkentést kapnak az olvashatóság megőrzése érdekében. A teljes effektus-veremnek interaktív képkockasebességet kell fenntartania (cél 120 Hz a támogatott hardveren) az Apple GPU-k csempe-alapú késleltetett renderelési jellemzőinek és a nulla-másolású IOSurface útvonalaknak a kihasználásával, ahol lehetséges.


must always be contained in a single index.html file

entries.answer:
```text
Build a single self-contained `index.html` file that implements an interactive reasoning accordion component with live step-state animations, smooth dynamic height transitions, and a physically inspired multilayer real-time refractive “liquid glass” material system. Include all HTML, CSS, JavaScript, shaders, UI state, rendering logic, animation logic, and embedded assets directly in this one file. Do not require external packages, CDNs, build tools, image assets, server endpoints, additional files, placeholder content, mock behavior, simulated output, or incomplete code. The finished file must run directly in a modern browser and provide the complete working component.

Create a full-page demo interface containing a reasoning accordion named `cot-message-chunk` with an internal rendering mode named `cot-v5`. The accordion must display a sequence of reasoning steps. Each step must support these runtime states:

- Pending: a neutral status indicator is visible.
- Running: display an animated circular spinner that visibly rotates at a stable frame rate.
- Complete: replace the spinner with an animated progress checkmark.
- Error: display a clear error-state icon and visual treatment.
- Collapsed: show only the step title, state indicator, and summary.
- Expanded: show the full step detail with a dynamically measured height transition.
- Streaming: support incremental appending of text into the detail region while preserving scrolling, height animation, and layout stability.

Use a data-driven JavaScript model for the accordion. Each step must include a unique identifier, title, summary, full detail text, state, timestamp or elapsed-duration value, and optional metadata. Render the complete accordion from this data structure. Provide controls inside the demo to start, pause, reset, complete, fail, expand, collapse, and stream content into individual reasoning steps. These controls must operate on the actual component state and must update the rendered UI immediately.

Implement dynamic height transitions without using fixed heights. Measure the content’s actual scroll height when opening or closing an item. Use JavaScript and CSS transitions so each item expands and collapses smoothly even when its content changes while expanded. Handle interruptions correctly: if a step is opened, closed, receives streamed text, or changes state before an existing transition completes, calculate the current rendered height and transition cleanly to the new target height without jumping, clipping, or leaving stale inline styles. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by minimizing or disabling nonessential movement while preserving state clarity.

Use a dark, high-contrast application background with independently moving visual content behind the glass components. The moving background is mandatory because the glass material must visibly react to the content underneath it. Construct the background in the same file using animated gradients, luminous blobs, geometric panels, scrolling text-like blocks, and contrast-varying regions. The background must continuously move beneath the accordion so that refraction, color tint, luminance adaptation, and distortion remain visibly responsive to the changing scene.

Do not implement ordinary glassmorphism. Do not rely on `backdrop-filter` as the primary optical mechanism. Implement refractive glass through a GPU-rendered WebGL2 or WebGPU pipeline. Prefer WebGL2 for broad browser compatibility. The glass surface must sample a captured or separately rendered background texture, distort sampling coordinates through an SDF-derived normal field, apply channel-separated refraction for chromatic dispersion, generate Fresnel edge response, render dynamic specular highlights, modulate blur by depth and signed distance, adapt tint to local luminance, and composite with correct premultiplied alpha.

Architect the liquid-glass renderer as a layered composition system equivalent to the following conceptual hierarchy, implemented in browser-compatible code and shaders:

1. Create a root glass-effect container that owns the complete visual stack for each glass element.
2. Support an optional parent wrapper that can coordinate multiple glass-element instances and allow their shapes to visually merge.
3. Create a primary backdrop sampling stage that captures or renders the content behind each glass element into a GPU texture. Maintain a unique compositing group identifier per glass group so multiple glass groups remain visually isolated.
4. Track local luminance continuously for each glass element. Expose equivalent runtime configuration fields:
   - `tracksLuma`: boolean controlling whether local luminance is sampled continuously.
   - `lumaSubrect`: normalized rectangle defining the background region used for luminance tracking.
   - `allowsFilteredLuma`: boolean controlling whether filtered black or white luminance overlays may be applied.
   - `lumaUpdateRate`: floating-point smoothing coefficient controlling temporal adaptation.
5. Generate an SDF texture source called `@0`. This source must represent the signed-distance-field geometry and an associated normal field for the active glass shapes.
6. Inside the SDF source, support one or more shape-element definitions. Each shape element must store a signed-distance representation of one rounded rectangle or other supported primitive.
7. Create two sibling highlight passes named `@1` and `@2`. These passes must reuse the primary SDF geometry without re-rasterizing it. Use them for directional edge-lighting and secondary highlight behavior.
8. Apply a primary compositing filter conceptually named `glassBackground`. It must consume the `@0` SDF/normal texture and use it to perform refraction, Gaussian or mip-based blur, vibrancy adjustment, tone mapping, adaptive tint, and chromatic dispersion.
9. Apply optional highlight color-matrix stages conceptually equivalent to `vibrantColorMatrix` so the directional highlight layers can receive independent color, intensity, and tonal control.

Implement the SDF processing system fully in shader code. Define all glass geometry using signed-distance functions. Include analytic SDF functions for rounded rectangles. Support configurable corner radius, independent width and height, soft inset, and optional superellipse behavior. Provide an SDF smooth-union operator that accepts two SDF values and a blend coefficient `k`, returning a continuous merged distance field. Use the smooth-union operation when neighboring accordion surfaces overlap or approach one another, so adjacent expanded accordion panels can morph and blend like a continuous liquid material rather than appearing as disconnected rectangles.

Calculate surface normals from the combined signed-distance field. Prefer analytic gradients where practical; otherwise use stable finite-difference gradients in the fragment shader. Use these normals for refraction direction, edge response, shadowing, and specular highlights. Ensure normal sampling remains stable across device pixel ratios and responsive layout changes.

Implement a full fragment-shader optical simulation. For every output fragment:

- Sample the dynamically rendered background texture.
- Evaluate the local SDF and derive its gradient and normalized surface normal.
- Determine whether the fragment lies inside, at the edge of, or outside the glass geometry.
- Calculate refracted sampling offsets from the normal field.
- Use GLSL refraction mathematics equivalent to the Metal `refract` function.
- Use separate refractive indices or channel-specific displacement scales for red, green, and blue to produce physically inspired chromatic aberration.
- Sample the red, green, and blue channels at independently refracted coordinates.
- Compute a Fresnel-style edge intensity from the view direction and surface normal using a Schlick-like approximation.
- Produce directional specular highlights based on the surface normal, a configurable dynamic light direction, roughness, shininess, and view direction.
- Generate at least two independent highlight lobes corresponding to the `@1` and `@2` highlight passes, with separate directions, colors, widths, and intensities.
- Perform mipmapped texture blur or multi-sample Gaussian blur. Modulate the blur radius by signed distance to the glass boundary, element size, local luminance, edge proximity, and scroll-edge state.
- Apply local luminance analysis to adapt tint, opacity, contrast, and shadow intensity. Dark underlying areas must cause the glass to brighten or lift its tint sufficiently for legibility; bright underlying areas must increase contrast and shift the tint/shadow treatment appropriately.
- Apply optional filtered luminance overlays when `allowsFilteredLuma` is enabled.
- Composite refraction, blurred background, internal tint, highlights, edge response, and shadow contribution into a final premultiplied-alpha output color.
- Preserve readable foreground text through contrast-aware text color selection, subtle text shadowing, and background-dependent opacity adjustment.

Use a dynamic light model. Track pointer position within the viewport and use it as a virtual device-tilt/light-direction input. The specular highlight must move continuously across each glass surface as the pointer moves. Add optional device-orientation support where available, but do not require permission-dependent motion data for the component to function. Smooth the light direction over time to avoid jitter. The light response must feel attached to the glass material rather than being a static gradient.

Create a glass material parameter object for every instance. Include at minimum:

- `opacity`
- `baseTint`
- `tintStrength`
- `refractionStrength`
- `redRefractionScale`
- `greenRefractionScale`
- `blueRefractionScale`
- `dispersionStrength`
- `blurRadius`
- `edgeBlurMultiplier`
- `fresnelPower`
- `fresnelStrength`
- `specularIntensity`
- `specularSharpness`
- `secondarySpecularIntensity`
- `shadowOpacity`
- `shadowBlur`
- `shadowOffset`
- `tracksLuma`
- `lumaSubrect`
- `allowsFilteredLuma`
- `lumaUpdateRate`
- `scrollEdgeBlurMultiplier`
- `scrollEdgeOpacityReduction`
- `smoothUnionRadius`
- `cornerRadius`
- `superellipseExponent`

Automatically adapt material parameters to geometry and background conditions. Larger panels must receive stronger diffusion, greater blur radius, deeper shadow, and proportionally adjusted refraction. Smaller panels must retain sharper edge definition. When an accordion item is close to a scrolling edge, increase blur and reduce opacity to preserve readability and reduce distracting contrast. Continuously smooth all automatic parameter changes so no visible popping occurs.

Render the accordion content above the glass surface while retaining the sense that content belongs inside the material. Place titles, summaries, step details, metadata, and state indicators in a foreground content layer. Ensure controls are accessible with keyboard navigation, visible focus states, semantic button elements, ARIA-expanded state, ARIA-controls relationships, and status announcements for state changes. Use readable typography with proper contrast across changing glass conditions.

Implement checkmark animation using SVG or CSS stroke animation. Animate the checkmark path only after a state enters `complete`. Implement spinner animation with a true rotating visual indicator while a state is `running`. Ensure state transitions animate smoothly but never obscure the actual state. Keep status icons and text distinct enough to remain understandable when motion reduction is enabled.

Use a rendering loop coordinated with `requestAnimationFrame`. Render at the display refresh rate where possible and avoid unnecessary layout reads, texture uploads, canvas resizing, and shader recompilation. Use a single shared WebGL context and batch all glass surfaces into one compositing pass where practical. Use offscreen canvases or framebuffers for the moving background and SDF data. Reuse textures, framebuffers, buffers, and shader programs. Render at device-pixel-ratio-aware resolution while exposing an internal quality scaler that can reduce render resolution if sustained frame time exceeds the target budget.

Ensure the implementation responds correctly to window resize, device pixel ratio changes, accordion expansion/collapse, streamed content updates, pointer movement, scroll movement, and reduced-motion preference changes. Construct the page in this order:
```

entries.query: now critique your answer and fix the weak parts
entries.answer:
The previous prompt was strong in scope but had several weaknesses: it asked for a sophisticated visual system without specifying a sufficiently realistic browser architecture, it ambiguously mixed browser implementation requirements with native-compositor concepts, and it did not strictly prevent a code generator from silently substituting fake visual effects for actual refraction. It also needed firmer acceptance criteria, a clearer rendering pipeline, explicit fallback boundaries, and tighter one-file delivery constraints.

## Weak points

| Weak point | Why it matters | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Native layer terminology was retained conceptually | Terms such as private compositor layers and filters can tempt an implementation to rely on unavailable APIs or to imitate them only nominally. | Define browser-native equivalents explicitly: WebGL2 textures, framebuffer passes, GLSL functions, and DOM geometry synchronization. |
| “Capture content behind it” was underspecified | A browser cannot generally read arbitrary composited DOM pixels behind a canvas. | Require that all refract-able background content be rendered into an owned WebGL background texture, while foreground accordion text remains DOM above the canvas. |
| Genuine refraction was not testable | A code generator could use `backdrop-filter`, static gradients, or a blurred pseudo-element and call it refraction. | Add non-negotiable acceptance checks: background texture must be sampled at displaced UV coordinates in GLSL; RGB channels must use distinct coordinates; no `backdrop-filter`. |
| Multi-element compositing was vague | Separate canvases or independent card shaders would not allow shapes to merge convincingly. | Require one shared full-viewport canvas, a unioned SDF field, and all glass regions rendered in the same composition pass. |
| SDF texture details were incomplete | The prompt said “SDF texture” but did not define texture formats, passes, channels, or coordinate mapping. | Specify a float/half-float-compatible offscreen field texture and define channel responsibilities. |
| Luminance tracking was not practical enough | “Continuously sample luminance” could become a costly GPU→CPU readback every frame. | Compute local luminance in the shader using low-frequency background data and only perform throttled readback for optional diagnostic UI. |
| Dynamic-height behavior needed a deterministic method | Generic “measure scroll height” instructions can create transition bugs when content changes during a transition. | Specify the exact interrupt-safe height-transition algorithm. |
| “No fake content” conflicted with a demo | A runnable demo needs visible reasoning steps, but should not pretend to be real model reasoning. | Require functional sample component data labeled as demonstration data, not fake processing output; all interactions must operate on live state. |
| Performance guidance lacked measurable thresholds | “Maintain 120 Hz” alone does not define how the system adapts when it cannot. | Require moving frame-time monitoring, quality tiers, and concrete degradation order. |
| Accessibility requirements needed verification | Mentioning ARIA is not enough to ensure a usable accordion. | Add keyboard and semantic acceptance criteria. |

## Revised comprehensive prompt

```text
Create exactly one complete, self-contained `index.html` file. The file must contain every required HTML element, CSS rule, JavaScript module, GLSL shader source string, SVG path, data object, and runtime asset inline. Do not use external libraries, package managers, CDNs, remote fonts, image URLs, import statements, build tools, server-side code, additional files, or network requests.

The file must run by opening it directly in a modern desktop browser that supports WebGL2. It must implement a fully functional interactive reasoning accordion component named `cot-message-chunk`, with a visual mode named `cot-v5`, rendered over a genuine browser-native liquid-glass material. The liquid glass must be rendered by WebGL2 shaders and must use actual texture-coordinate displacement to refract a dynamically rendered background scene. Do not use `backdrop-filter`, CSS blur as the primary glass effect, a static image background, static gradient overlays pretending to be refraction, or any unavailable/native/private platform API.

The implementation must use this architecture:

1. DOM application layer:
   - Create an accessible HTML application shell.
   - Create a full-viewport background canvas for WebGL2 rendering.
   - Create a DOM overlay containing the reasoning accordion and its controls.
   - Render all interactive text, buttons, headings, metadata, focus outlines, status labels, and accessibility semantics in DOM.
   - Render the liquid-glass material only in the shared WebGL2 canvas below the DOM content.
   - Synchronize every accordion panel’s DOM bounding rectangle into the WebGL renderer each frame or whenever layout changes.

2. Shared renderer:
   - Create exactly one shared WebGL2 context.
   - Use one full-viewport canvas.
   - Render all visible glass panels through a shared compositing pipeline so their signed-distance fields can merge.
   - Do not create a separate WebGL canvas per accordion item.
   - Reuse GPU buffers, programs, textures, framebuffers, and vertex arrays.
   - Do not compile shaders, allocate textures, rebuild DOM trees, or perform repeated document queries inside the animation loop.

3. Refract-able background scene:
   - The glass can only refract content that is available as a GPU texture.
   - Build the complete background scene inside WebGL2 and render it to a background framebuffer texture before rendering glass.
   - The background scene must visibly move and vary behind the accordion. Include animated gradient fields, multiple moving luminous blobs, large high-contrast geometric bands, fine visual grain, and animated text-like rectangular content blocks.
   - Move at least some background content continuously beneath every glass surface so refractive displacement, chromatic dispersion, and luminance adaptation are clearly observable.
   - Do not claim to refract arbitrary DOM content. The WebGL-rendered background texture is the refracted source.

4. Accordion component:
   - Render a data-driven accordion from a JavaScript array of step objects.
   - Every step object must contain:
     - `id`
     - `title`
     - `summary`
     - `detail`
     - `state`
     - `elapsed`
     - `metadata`
     - `expanded`
   - Support these states:
     - `pending`
     - `running`
     - `complete`
     - `error`
     - `streaming`
   - Each step must contain a semantic button used as the accordion trigger.
   - Use `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, a unique detail-region ID, a visible keyboard focus indicator, and a keyboard-operable interface.
   - Enter and Space must toggle focused accordion items.
   - Include an `aria-live="polite"` status area announcing state changes without repeatedly announcing animation frames.
   - Display:
     - Step title.
     - Compact summary.
     - State indicator.
     - Elapsed time or timestamp.
     - Optional metadata.
     - Expandable full detail region.
   - Display a true animated spinner for `running` and `streaming`.
   - Display an animated SVG checkmark for `complete`.
   - Display a clearly distinct error indicator for `error`.
   - Do not represent any status only through color.

5. Functional component controls:
   - Add real controls to:
     - Start a selected step.
     - Pause streaming.
     - Resume streaming.
     - Mark a selected step complete.
     - Mark a selected step as error.
     - Reset all steps.
     - Expand all steps.
     - Collapse all steps.
     - Toggle dynamic device-light simulation.
   - Controls must mutate the real JavaScript step model and immediately update the actual DOM and WebGL geometry.
   - Include a small, clearly labeled demonstration data set with multiple reasoning steps. Label this content as component demonstration data. Do not imply it is hidden model reasoning or real-time internal reasoning.
   - Initialize at least:
     - One pending item.
     - One running item.
     - One completed item.
     - One error item.
     - One expanded item.
     - One streaming item that appends visible text fragments over time to its own detail region.
   - The streaming behavior must append from a predefined in-file text sequence and must be pausable and resumable.

6. Interrupt-safe dynamic-height animation:
   - Do not use fixed expanded heights.
   - Use the following exact algorithm whenever an item opens, closes, or changes content while open:
     1. Read the detail panel’s current computed pixel height.
     2. Cancel or replace any existing height transition without snapping.
     3. Set the current pixel height as an inline style.
     4. Force the browser to recognize that height before applying the target height.
     5. For expansion, calculate the target from the panel’s actual `scrollHeight`.
     6. For collapse, calculate target height `0`.
     7. Animate height with a CSS transition using a cubic-bezier timing curve.
     8. On transition completion, remove the explicit height for an expanded item and retain height `0` for a collapsed item.
     9. If content streams while expanded, animate from its current rendered height to its new `scrollHeight`.
     10. If the operation is interrupted, begin the replacement transition from the current computed height rather than the old target.
   - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. In reduced-motion mode, remove continuous decorative movement where practical, use immediate or short state transitions, and preserve all state information.

7. Browser-native liquid-glass model:
   - Treat each accordion panel as a 2D lens defined by a signed-distance field.
   - Construct a conceptual effect hierarchy in JavaScript:
     - Root glass-effect group.
     - Optional multi-panel grouping wrapper.
     - Primary backdrop texture sampling pass.
     - SDF field pass named `@0`.
     - Two highlight field passes named `@1` and `@2`.
     - Final composite pass conceptually named `glassBackground`.
   - These names are internal JavaScript identifiers only. They must not depend on unavailable browser APIs.
   - The `@0` pass must provide a field used to determine the unioned panel geometry and normal data.
   - The `@1` and `@2` passes must reuse the same geometry data and create independent directional highlight behavior without independently redefining the shapes.

8. Glass material configuration:
   - Create a material parameter object for each glass panel. Include:
     - `opacity`
     - `baseTint`
     - `tintStrength`
     - `refractionStrength`
     - `redRefractionScale`
     - `greenRefractionScale`
     - `blueRefractionScale`
     - `dispersionStrength`
     - `blurRadius`
     - `edgeBlurMultiplier`
     - `fresnelPower`
     - `fresnelStrength`
     - `specularIntensity`
     - `specularSharpness`
     - `secondarySpecularIntensity`
     - `shadowOpacity`
     - `shadowBlur`
     - `shadowOffset`
     - `tracksLuma`
     - `lumaSubrect`
     - `allowsFilteredLuma`
     - `lumaUpdateRate`
     - `scrollEdgeBlurMultiplier`
     - `scrollEdgeOpacityReduction`
     - `smoothUnionRadius`
     - `cornerRadius`
     - `superellipseExponent`
   - Provide a visible debug-free runtime configuration area in the interface for changing at least refraction strength, blur radius, tint strength, dispersion strength, smooth-union radius, and light intensity.
   - Parameter controls must alter the rendered material immediately.

9. SDF geometry:
   - Define all glass geometry with GLSL signed-distance functions.
   - Implement an analytic rounded-rectangle SDF accepting center, half-size, and corner radius.
   - Implement optional superellipse behavior controlled by `superellipseExponent`.
   - Implement a smooth-union function accepting two signed-distance values and a blend radius `k`.
   - Use smooth union to merge nearby or overlapping accordion panels into continuous liquid-glass geometry.
   - Derive surface normals from the combined SDF with centered finite differences in screen-space coordinates.
   - Make the finite-difference distance scale resolution-aware so normals remain stable at different device pixel ratios.
   - Use the same combined SDF for shape masking, edge response, blur modulation, shadowing, refraction, and specular lighting.

10. Required render passes:
   - Background pass:
     - Render the moving background scene to a full-resolution framebuffer texture.
     - Generate mipmaps for this texture after the background pass.
   - Glass field/composite pass:
     - Render the full viewport.
     - Evaluate all active panel SDFs in a fragment shader.
     - Smooth-union panel geometry where panel bounds overlap or approach within the configured merge radius.
     - Sample the background framebuffer at displaced coordinates.
     - Draw the final glass surface only inside or around the combined SDF shape.
   - Optional performance pass:
     - Maintain a reduced-resolution render target when quality scaling is required.
     - Upscale it with a final compositing pass while retaining crisp DOM text above the canvas.

11. Required fragment-shader behavior:
   - Sample the moving background framebuffer texture.
   - Evaluate the local combined SDF at the fragment’s viewport coordinate.
   - Derive a normalized surface normal from the SDF gradient.
   - Calculate an interior/edge mask from signed distance and anti-alias it with `fwidth`.
   - Implement refraction through displaced texture coordinates.
   - Implement separate red, green, and blue refractive sampling coordinates:
     - Red must use its own displacement scale.
     - Green must use its own displacement scale.
     - Blue must use its own displacement scale.
   - Combine channel-separated samples into a chromatically dispersed refracted color.
   - Use GLSL’s `refract` function or mathematically equivalent vector refraction behavior.
   - Calculate Fresnel response using a Schlick-like function based on the surface normal and a view direction.
   - Generate a primary specular highlight controlled by dynamic light direction, surface normal, sharpness, and intensity.
   - Generate a secondary independent directional highlight corresponding to `@2`.
   - Modulate highlight width and intensity near the SDF edge.
   - Perform mip-based blur through explicit `textureLod` sampling from background mip levels, or through a compact weighted multi-sample blur if mip-level selection is not available.
   - Increase blur near edges, for larger panels, and in configured scroll-edge regions.
   - Reduce opacity near configured scroll-edge regions.
   - Calculate local luminance from the sampled background color in shader using a perceptual luminance formula.
   - Smooth luminance adaptation over time in JavaScript uniforms or through a history texture. Do not perform blocking per-frame GPU-to-CPU pixel readback for core rendering.
   - Use local luminance to adapt tint, opacity, contrast, and shadow:
     - Dark backgrounds must create enough lift and tint to preserve text readability.
     - Bright backgrounds must increase contrast separation and adjust tint/shadow accordingly.
   - When `allowsFilteredLuma` is enabled, allow a controlled black or white luminance overlay based on local luminance.
   - Output correctly premultiplied alpha:
     - RGB output must already be multiplied by alpha.
     - Configure blending consistently for premultiplied-alpha composition.

12. Dynamic lighting:
   - Use pointer position as the primary virtual device-tilt source.
   - Convert pointer position to a normalized light vector.
   - Smooth light motion with interpolation to avoid jitter.
   - Make specular highlights visibly shift as the pointer moves.
   - Add optional `DeviceOrientationEvent` support if available and permitted, but never make device orientation mandatory.
   - Provide a control that toggles pointer/device-light response on and off.
   - In reduced-motion mode, retain a stable fixed light direction or significantly reduce motion.

13. Adaptive material behavior:
   - Update material values from panel geometry and background conditions:
     - Larger panels receive greater blur, slightly stronger scattering, and deeper shadow.
     - Smaller panels retain sharper internal detail and tighter highlights.
     - Panels near the top or bottom viewport scroll boundary receive more blur and lower opacity.
     - Strong local luminance contrast modifies tint strength and shadow opacity.
   - Smooth all adaptive values over time; do not visibly pop between states.
   - Keep DOM text legible by choosing foreground text color from panel luminance class and applying a subtle text shadow only when necessary.

14. Performance requirements:
   - Use `requestAnimationFrame`.
   - Track instantaneous frame duration and a rolling moving average.
   - Target 120 Hz when the display and browser permit it.
   - Treat 8.33 ms as the 120 Hz frame-time target and 16.67 ms as the 60 Hz fallback target.
   - If sustained average frame time exceeds the target budget, degrade quality in this order:
     1. Reduce background render target resolution.
     2. Reduce blur sample count or mip detail.
     3. Reduce visual grain complexity.
     4. Reduce maximum active SDF panel count processed at full precision only if necessary.
   - If performance recovers, restore quality gradually.
   - Do not sacrifice accordion interaction, accessibility, dynamic height correctness, or text readability during quality reduction.
   - Use device-pixel-ratio-aware sizing with a capped internal render scale.
   - Use `ResizeObserver` for accordion geometry changes and `window` resize handling for viewport changes.
   - Use retained element references rather than querying the DOM every frame.

15. Styling and layout:
   - Build a responsive layout that works from narrow mobile-width viewports to wide desktop viewports.
   - Keep the accordion centered within a readable maximum width.
   - Use a coherent dark interface palette that allows the moving background and glass refraction to remain visible.
   - Ensure DOM text remains crisp because it is not rendered through the WebGL blur pass.
   - Ensure buttons remain visually distinct from the glass panels.
   - Use no external font dependency; use a robust system font stack.
   - Include CSS fallback styling for environments where WebGL2 cannot initialize:
     - The accordion must remain fully interactive.
     - The fallback may use a simpler translucent CSS surface.
     - The fallback must not claim to provide the shader-based refractive effect.

16. Acceptance criteria:
   - The result is exactly one `index.html` file.
   - Opening the file locally produces a complete interactive page.
   - No network request is necessary for visible operation.
   - The reasoning accordion supports all required states and real control-driven transitions.
   - Streaming visibly appends to one expanded detail region and height adapts without clipping or jumps.
   - The spinner rotates while active.
   - The checkmark animates when completion occurs.
   - Keyboard navigation and ARIA accordion semantics work.
   - Pointer movement visibly changes highlight direction.
   - Moving background content visibly refracts through the glass panels.
   - Red, green, and blue channels visibly separate subtly at high-contrast refractive edges when dispersion is increased.
   - Nearby expanded panels visibly merge through smooth SDF union when the merge radius is increased.
   - The implementation contains actual shader texture-coordinate displacement and does not use `backdrop-filter`.
   - All required functionality is implemented as working production-ready code, not prose, TODO comments, stubs, placeholders, simulated UI controls, or incomplete fragments.

Return only the complete contents of the final `index.html` file. Do not add commentary, setup instructions, explanations, markdown fences, or any text outside the HTML document.
```
